instrument: Prakriti Parikshan (Vata / Pitta / Kapha), 40-item Govardhan School of Yoga workbook
note: Percentages are each dosha's points out of 80 (see prakriti.json scoring_notes: 2 pts per single tick, 1 pt each for a double tick). Dual-dosha combinations are the norm, not the exception — the synthesis prompt should default to checking for a blend before declaring a single dominant type. A separate short-term Vikriti check (prakriti.json vikriti_check) should be read alongside this result but scored and reported separately, never merged into these percentages.

VAT.label: Vata
VAT.description: Light, quick, variable. When strong: creative, quick-thinking, adaptable, but prone to restlessness, irregular routines, and anxiety under stress.

PIT.label: Pitta
PIT.description: Sharp, warm, intense. When strong: focused, driven, decisive, but prone to irritability, impatience, and burning out under pressure.

KAP.label: Kapha
KAP.description: Heavy, steady, slow. When strong: calm, grounded, loyal, but prone to inertia, resistance to change, and low motivation to start things.

dominance_patterns.label: {dosha}-dominant
dominance_patterns.description: A clear single constitutional tendency; the described traits and imbalance-patterns for that dosha apply fairly directly.

dominance_patterns.condition: two doshas each >= 30%, within 15 points of each other
dominance_patterns.label: {dosha_a}-{dosha_b} (dual)
dominance_patterns.description: The most common pattern — traits from both doshas show up, often in different contexts (e.g. one under stress, the other at rest).

dominance_patterns.label: Tridoshic
dominance_patterns.description: Rare and worth flagging as notable — no single dosha leads; likely to feel different from day to day depending on season, sleep, and stress.
